title: Checkpoint 0: Hans vs Stockfish (skill 0)
notes: Checkpoint after game 0, from the Italian Game: Hans plays the yardstick, Stockfish at skill 0. Nothing is studied afterwards.

moves.thought: This is the Giuoco Piano main line; after 4...Nf6 the critical central break is d4, striking at e5 while my c3 pawn supports the recapture. After 5.d4 exd4 6.cxd4 Bb4+ 7.Bd2 (or Nc3) I get a strong pawn centre, and 5...Nxe4 6.d5 regains the piece favourably.

Black's 5...Bd6 is passive and blocks the d-pawn, so I want to open the center immediately with dxe5, when every recapture costs Black time (after ...Nxe5 Nxe5 Bxe5 I gain tempo with f4/e5). Note that the greedy 6...Nxe4 fails to 7.Bxf7+ Kxf7 8.Qd5+ regaining the piece.

Black's bishop on e5 is loose, so I checked the forcing sequence 7.Bxf7+ Kxf7 8.Nxe5+ Nxe5 9.Qd5+ (king must move, nothing can block or defend e5) 10.Qxe5, which nets a clean extra pawn with Black's king stuck on f8/g6 and his rooks unable to connect. Declining with 7...Kf8 or 7...Ke7 also loses a pawn after 8.Nxe5 Nxe5 9.Bd5/Bb3, so the combination works in all lines.

I gave up the bishop on f7, so I must regain material immediately: Nxe5+ wins the bishop back, and after ...Nxe5 the fork Qd5+ picks up the knight on e5, leaving me a clean pawn up with Black's king stranded. If Black declines with a king move instead, I'm simply two pawns ahead with a dominant centre.

I'm currently a piece down for a pawn, but the point of the combination is 9.Qd5+, which forks the king on f7 and the undefended knight on e5 — nothing can block on e6 and no king move defends e5. So after any reply I recapture with Qxe5, emerging a clean pawn up with a safe position.

Having given up my queen in the forced sequence, I must at least recapture the knight on d5 to stay only a queen down for two pawns rather than losing material for nothing. The pawn on d5 also gains space and takes the c6/e6 squares, and no black capture or check hits me immediately after it.

I'm down a queen for a pawn after the unsound sacrifices, so I need to get my remaining pieces coordinated and the king safe rather than lash out. Bf4 invites the annoying 11...Nd3+, and f4 runs into Nd3+ too, so I'll castle, keeping f2 protected by the rook and preparing Re1, Nd2 and Bf4 next.

I'm down a queen for a pawn, so I need activity and to trade off Black's strong knight on e5. Re1 develops with tempo on the knight, and if Nd3 then Re3 harasses it again (Nxb2 would just lose the knight to Bxb2), whereas Bf4 immediately allows Nd3 hitting both my bishop and the loose b2 pawn.

I'm down heavy material after the queen trade went wrong, so I need active development and to keep pieces on to create practical chances. Bf4 develops with tempo, adding a second attacker to the e5 knight (only defended by the d6 pawn), so Black must move it or defend it; Nd3 fails to Rxd3 and Nf3+ fails to gxf3.

I'm down a lot of material after the queen trade misfire, so I need to grab what I can: the e5 knight is attacked twice (Bf4 and Re1) and defended only by the d6 pawn, so Bxe5 dxe5 Rxe5 nets me a pawn, trades off an attacker, and leaves my rook active on the open e-file with a passed d-pawn. Alternatives like Re4 don't win a4 since it's defended by the a8 rook, and after Rxe5 the recapture Qf6 just chases my rook to safety.

I'm down a queen and bishop for a knight, so I need material back and activity wherever I can get it. Rxe5 grabs the free e5 pawn (the knight that defended it is gone), and although Qf6 or Qd6 will chase my rook, I can retreat to e1 or e2 while keeping f2 covered. Grabbing the pawn and keeping my rooks active is the only practical try.

I'm down heavy material after the earlier queen misstep, so I need my rook active and safe rather than hanging on e5 where ...Qd6/...Re6 hits it. Re4 centralises, steps off the loose square, and attacks the stray a4 pawn, so if Black grabs d5 with ...Rd6 I regain a pawn with Rxa4.

I'm down a queen and bishop for two knights after the earlier sacrifices, so my priority is grabbing material back and simplifying. Rxa4 picks up the loose a-pawn and offers a rook trade (17...Rxa4 18.Rxa4), whereas Re7+ just drops the rook to Kxe7 or Qxe7.

I'm down material, so I need to hold my only asset, the advanced d5 pawn, and get pieces active. Nd2 would allow ...Qd6 followed by ...Qxd5, so I prefer Rd4, which defends d5, centralizes the rook safely (the queen's file pressure is blocked by my own pawn), and keeps Nd2-e4 as the follow-up.

I'm down heavy material, so I need to develop my last piece and build a solid blockade around the strong d5 passer. Nd2 brings the knight out with Ne4 (hitting the f6 rook) or Nb3–c5 ideas, and the rook on d4 covers d2 against any Qa5 tricks while still guarding d5.

I'm down material, so I need activity and tempo: Ne4 attacks the f6 rook, and defending it with the king doesn't help since Nxf6 wins rook for knight. Note Black can't challenge with Re6 or Rc6 because the d5 pawn covers both squares, and Rf5 runs into Ng3 hitting rook and h5.

Black's rook on f6 is attacked by my knight; although it's defended three times, Nxf6 simply wins a rook for the knight, cutting into Black's material edge. I checked the alternatives: Nd6+ fails to cxd6, and Ng5+ just lets the rook escape, while 21. d6 cxd6 22. Nxd6+ Ke7 23. Nxc8+ Qxc8 is only an even trade.

I'm down material (Q+R+B vs two rooks and three extra pawns), so I need my passed d-pawn and active rooks to generate counterplay. Rad1 doubles on the d-file behind the passer and sets up the real threat of d6, since after cxd6 Rxd6+ Qxd6 Rxd6+ I'd win the queen for a rook and pawn. It also keeps everything defended with no checks or captures available for Black.

Black's bishop on d7 is defended only by the queen, and both my rooks are stacked behind the d5 pawn, so pushing d6 opens the file: after 23...cxd6 24.Rxd6 I threaten 25.Rxd7 Qxd7 26.Rxd7, winning queen and bishop for a rook, while 24...Bmoves allows 25.Rxd8 Rxd8 26.Rxd8 with rook and six pawns against bishop and three. If Black tries 23...Qxd6 24.Rxd6 cxd6 25.Rxd6 I regain the piece-for-pawn balance with an easy three-pawn plus, and 23...Bf5 24.dxc7 gives me a monster pawn.

My d6 wedge is safe (both rooks guard it and the bishop on d7 can't leave without dropping the queen to Qxd6 Rxd6), but my a2 pawn is a long-term target for the black queen, so I want to resolve the queenside now. 24. a4 either liquidates my weakest pawn after bxa4 Rxa4 with an active rook, or after 24...b4 25. cxb4 gives me connected queenside passers; I avoided Rf4+ since Ke5 or Kg5 just hits the rook (c3 guards b4/d4, not f4), and Rd5/Rc4/Ra4 drop a rook to cxd5 or bxc4/bxa4.

My a4 pawn is hanging to the queen, so I want to resolve the queenside at once; axb5 trades it off and, if Black answers cxb5, the c6 pawn disappears so Qd5 and cxd5 ideas vanish and my rooks get the d5/e-file squares. After that I plan Re4 and Re7, hitting the loose bishop on d7 and the g7 pawn while my d6 pawn remains a thorn.

I'm down material, so I need activity: Rd5 hits the queen on b5 along the fifth rank, simultaneously attacks the h5 pawn, and backs up my strong d6 pawn while keeping my rooks connected on the d-file. If Black tries to defend with Rb8, Rxb5 trades my rook for the queen, so the queen must step aside and I pick up h5 (with Rxh8 ideas) to get my pawns rolling.

Black's queen on b2 is eyeing both c3 and f2, so I want a setup that holds everything while keeping my passed d6-pawn alive; Rf5+ loses to Kxf5 and Rxh5 loses to Rxh5. R5d3 defends c3 along the third rank, keeps d6 protected, keeps both rooks mutually connected with no back-rank check (Rd1 stays home), and if the queen tries Qc2 I simply answer R1d2 hitting it again.

My rook on d1 is attacked by the queen, so I need to keep it guarded while gaining a tempo; R3d2 hits the queen on e2, is defended by Rd1, still guards the d6 pawn down the open file, and crucially Rd1 covers e1 so there's no ...Qe1+ trick (and ...Qxf2+ simply runs into Rxf2).

I'm down material, so my only real counterplay is the passed d6 pawn — c4 prepares c5 to create connected passers backed by both rooks. Usefully, if Black grabs at the pawn with Qe4 or Qa4, my Rd4 both defends c4 and attacks the queen along the fourth rank, and Qe1+ just loses the queen to Rxe1.

I'm down material, so I want the most solid structure possible: c5 builds a mutually-defended c5/d6 pawn duo (d6 guards c5, both rooks guard d6), which Black can't attack profitably — Qxc5 dxc5 or Qxd6 Rxd6 just lose the queen — and it keeps the bishop on d7 tied to stopping the pawn. The active try Rd5 looked tempting with Rxh5, but after ...Qa5 or ...Be6 my rook gets traded off and that only helps Black.

Black's main threat is Qd8-a5, hitting the undefended c5 pawn (and d2), after which my c5/d6 wedge — my only real asset — collapses; Rd5 would defend c5 but gets kicked by Be6. Rc2 solidly guards c5 from behind, keeps Rd1 holding the first rank and behind the passer, and the d6 pawn stays tactically immune since any capture on d6 is answered by cxd6.

I'm down heavy material (Q+R+B vs two rooks), so my only hope is the solid mutual-defence setup where Rc2 guards c5 and Rd1 guards d6 — moves like Rd5 lose instantly to cxd5, and Rcd2 drops c5 to ...Qb6. So I make a useful waiting move, giving my king luft and preventing ...g4/...h4 ideas while keeping both rooks on their defensive posts.

Black is up material, so I need activity: my c2 rook is passive and vulnerable to Bf5, so I swing it to c4 where it controls the fourth rank and can jump to e4/f4/g4 against Black's loose king. Crucially, Black's bishop and queen are tied to stopping d7 — the moment the bishop leaves d7, I push d7 (defended by Rd1) and Black's queen is frozen on d8.

I'm down material (Q+B for a rook), so my only real asset is the c5/d6 pawn duo — and Rg4/Rh4/Rf4/Re4 all drop a rook to gxf4/hxg4/Bxe4, while immediate d7 just loses a pawn to Bxd7. Rc3 keeps the c5 pawn defended along the file, stays safe from everything, and prepares Rd3 to double on the d-file so that d7 becomes a real threat (then Bxd7 Rxd7 Qxd7 Rxd7 wins material for me).

I'm down material, so my priority is holding the c5/d6 pawn wedge and keeping Black's pawn breaks under control; Rd4 doubles the defense of d6 (any ...Rd7/...Rxd6 sequence ends with my Rd1 picking up the queen), stays off the bishop's diagonals, and importantly covers g4 so that ...g5-g4 hxg4 hxg4 just drops the pawn to Rxg4+. Pushing d7 fails since the bishop, rook on h7 and queen all cover that square, and h4/g4 would loosen my king's shelter.

My rooks are tied down but perfectly placed — Rd4 guards the d6 wedge and Rc3 guards c5, so moves like f4 or d7 just drop a pawn (36.d7 Bxd7 or 36.f4 gxf4 37.Rxf4 Qxd6). Instead I improve my king: Kh2 steps off the first rank, kills any ...Rb1+ ideas, and defends g2 against a future ...Bf5-e4.

My c5/d6 pawn chain is my only real counterplay (c5 is guarded by Rc3, and c5 in turn guards d6), so I want to keep Rc3 in place and activate the other rook. Re4 hits the undefended bishop on e6 and gains a tempo; if Black answers Bd5 I can go Re5, hitting both the bishop and g5, and Rd3 next to pile on d5.

I'm down material (two rooks against queen, rook and bishop), so my immediate concern is the undefended f2 pawn that Black's rook on f7 is eyeing; f4 loses a rook to gxf4 and Rf4 drops to the g5 pawn too. Playing f3 shores up the pawn solidly (it's covered by g2) and keeps my rooks flexible behind the c5/d6 pawn duo.

My rook on c3 is attacked by the queen on a5, and the c5 pawn is also loose, so I want a move that solves both. Rcc4 puts the rooks side by side on the fourth rank where they defend each other and the c5 pawn, keeping my c5/d6 duo intact; tactical tries like Re6+ fail to Bxe6 and Re7 fails to Rxe7 dxe7 Qxc3 since the bishop covers e8.

The key tactical point is that Red4 hits the undefended queen on d2 along the d-file while the rook itself is protected by Rc4, so Qxd4 just loses the queen to Rxd4. It also keeps both rooks abreast on the fourth rank guarding c5 and d4, whereas tempting tries like Re6+ or Re7 simply drop material to Bxe6/Rxe7, and trading a pair of rooks only helps Black's queen.

Black's queen eyes my Rc4 along the a2-b3-c4 diagonal, so my d-rook must stay on the fourth rank to defend it, which rules out Rd5/Rd3/Rd2/Rd1; meanwhile my c5/d6 duo is solidly held (c5 covers d6, Rc4 covers c5). So instead of pure waiting I strike at Black's only real pawn asset: 41.h4 wins a pawn after gxh4 42.Rxh4 (still guarding c4 along the rank), and if 41...g4 42.fxg4 hxg4 43.Rxg4+ Black is left with just the c6 pawn, which kills his winning chances.

I'm down material, so my priority is a solid fortress holding c5 and d6 while keeping f3 and my king safe. Rc3 defends c5 along the file and f3 along the third rank, and it pre-empts Black's annoying ...Be6 hitting the undefended rook on c4; Rd4 stays safe since the a7-g1 diagonal is blocked by my own c5 pawn.

Black's immediate threat is ...gxh4, since my h4 pawn is undefended and my rooks can't recapture there; 43.g3 shores it up, keeps the g5 pawn under tension, and prepares to open the g-file favourably if Black ever takes (gxh4 gxh4 leaves my rooks eyeing his exposed king). I rejected Rd5 because cxd5 simply wins a rook, and Rf4/Rg4 drop material to Rxf4 or hxg4.

I'm down material, so my job is to hold the c5/d6 pawn chain and keep Black's queen out; the pawn moves (hxg5, f4, g4) only loosen my structure and open lines to my king. Rd2 keeps the second rank sealed (any queen incursion like Qa2 or Rb2 gets captured), supports the key Rd4 which guards both c5 and d6, and unlike Rc2 it can't be harassed by ...Bf5.

My pawns on c5 and d6 aren't actually attacked, so my rooks are free to get active, and Black's bishop on d7 is undefended (the c6 pawn blocks the queen's a4–d7 diagonal). With Re3 I threaten Re7 hitting the bishop, and if the bishop ever steps off d7 I get the strong push d7 trading my pawn for a rook; meanwhile h4 is still safely guarded by g3 so Qxh4+ is impossible.

I noticed Black's g5-pawn is completely undefended (my h4-pawn attacks it, and the light-squared bishop can never guard a dark square), so Rd5 adds a second attacker along the fifth rank while still covering d6 and leaving Re3 to guard f3. If Black defends with Rg8 I take with hxg5 (the pawn is then protected by Rd5), and after ...Qd1 or ...Be6 I simply grab with Rxg5, which is safe thanks to h4 and threatens Rxh5+.

Both blocking tries (Rd2 and Re2) simply drop a rook since neither square is defended — Qxd2 or Qxe2 wins material outright. So I must step out of the check, and Kg1 keeps the king off the long diagonal and away from potential Bf5+/h-file tricks that arise after Kh1 and a later Kh3.

Rd1 and Re1 both just drop a rook to Qxd1+/Qxe1+ since neither rook defends the other on the first rank, so I must step the king aside. Kf2 is best because it also shields f2 and gives the Re3 rook king support, keeping my f3 pawn chain solid while I prepare to push the d-pawn.

Black's queen check on b2 can be blocked with Re2, where the rook is protected by my king on f2, so Qxe2+ Kxe2 would simply win the queen for a rook. Re2 also keeps my strong rook on d5 supporting the c5/d6 passed pawns, unlike a king retreat which would let the checks continue.

Rxf3+ must simply be recaptured — Kg1, Kg2 or Ke1 all drop the e2 rook to Qxe2 (with check in two cases), while Kxf3 regains the rook so I have two rooks and four pawns against queen, bishop and three pawns. If Black tries Qc3+ I can block with Re3 or step back to Kf2, and Qxe2+ Kxe2 would leave me a clean rook-for-bishop up with an extra pawn.

Rd3 just drops the rook to Qxd3+ since e2 doesn't cover d3, and Ke4 walks into Bf5+/Qc4+ tactics. Kg2 steps out of the check safely — Black has no follow-up check (rank 2 is blocked by my rook on e2, rank 3 by my g3 pawn), and both my rooks and the c5/d6 pawn duo stay intact.

I'm down a queen for a rook, so I just need to grab material and keep my king safe; Re8+ fails to Bxe8 and c6 loses the pawn to Bxc6. hxg5 wins a pawn cleanly without exposing my king to immediate checks.

I'm down a queen for a rook, so my only practical chance is the c5/d6 pawn duo — passive play just loses to ...d3 and the queen rounding up my pawns. c6 hits the bishop immediately and, if the bishop takes, I get rook checks on the eighth rank with d6-d7 ideas; waiting moves give Black a free hand.

I must answer the bishop check on the long diagonal; blocking with Re4 just drops the rook to Bxe4+, so the king must step off the diagonal. Kh2 is best because it keeps the g3 pawn defended (after Kf2/Kg1 Black grabs it with Qxg3+ and keeps checking), and the rook on e2 stays flexible against the advancing d-pawn.

My rook on e2 is attacked by the d3 pawn, so it must move; Re8+ looks tempting but the bishop on c6 covers e8 and would simply capture. Rd2 both saves the rook and blocks/attacks the dangerous d3 passer, and neither the queen (from b3) nor the bishop can reach d2.

I noticed Black is threatening ...Qh1#, since the bishop on c6 covers h1 right through d5 and my rook on d2 can only reach g2, not h1. Kg1 keeps the rook guarding g2 (so ...Qg2+ is met by Rxg2) while giving the king the f2 flight square after ...Qh1+, and it still maintains the blockade of the d3 pawn.

I'm in check on the e3-g1 diagonal, and with the king moves (Kf1/Kh2) Black wins my undefended rook with Qe3 or Qf2+ followed by Qxd2, so I must interpose. Rf2 blocks safely — Qxf2+ is met by Kxf2, trading queen for rook in my favour — and after ...d2 I still have the resource Rf8+ followed by Rd8 to blockade the d-file and support my d6 pawn.

My rook on f2 is pinned by the queen on d4 against my king on g1, and Black threatens both Qxf2+ and d1=Q, so I must move the king; Kf1 allows d1=Q+ with immediate check, while Kh2 steps off the d4-g1 diagonal, unpinning the rook so that Rxd2 becomes a genuine threat. Black can still grab the rook with Qxf2+, but Kh2 is the only try that keeps any material and forces him to prove it.

I'm lost — Black's two queens will mate after any quiet move (Qxf2+ or Qh1#), so my only practical chance is a perpetual-check attempt with the rook, which the g5 pawn supports on f6. After Rf8+ Kh7 Rf7+ Kg6 Rf6+ I can keep checking forever; only Kg7 refutes it.

My rook on f8 is attacked by the king, so it must move, and Rd8/Re8/Rc8/Rf-squares are all covered by the queens or bishop (Rf7+/Rg8+/Rh8 just lose it to Kxf7 etc.). Rb8 is a safe square that also guards d8, so if I ever get d7 in, the promotion is supported and Qxd8 Rxd8 would win a queen for the rook.
